### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94608a7d72ecef7bf61d10dbab3bd80aea311055` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b221c59fe88b5bbbf9c4424d1946a624a7cf036d` — the merge of head `8ebaf237c4f1c26060891f62dfa990547b82aa7a` into base `94608a7d72ecef7bf61d10dbab3bd80aea311055`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b221c59fe88b5bbbf9c4424d1946a624a7cf036d && git checkout b221c59fe88b5bbbf9c4424d1946a624a7cf036d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 94608a7d72ecef7bf61d10dbab3bd80aea311055 8ebaf237c4f1c26060891f62dfa990547b82aa7a && git checkout -B drift-repro 94608a7d72ecef7bf61d10dbab3bd80aea311055 && git merge --no-ff 8ebaf237c4f1c26060891f62dfa990547b82aa7a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94608a7d72ecef7bf61d10dbab3bd80aea311055
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8ebaf237c4f1c26060891f62dfa990547b82aa7a`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #20901 (body; every comment — triage `5916820410`, claim `5916997003`, dev reports `5918594163` / `5920703403` / `5925602674`, seat rulings `5918621378` / `5920724494` / `5925624097`, landing records `5919493523` and `5921552300` as corrected, dispatch note `5924906441`), the at-tier record `5921114874` on PR #20953 (its ③ item 4 is this fragment's source), PRs #20927 and #20953 (bodies, merged as `bee75cebe6` and `c6b3a01d5d`), PR #21090 (body, file list: 2 files, +41 / −0), the net diff `origin/main...8ebaf237c4` (merge base `dff98c1f51`, which the head merges as its second parent; the one source commit is `51fcedaa0b`), the two D3 entry sources, the declared-type entry `18.inline-grid-column-currency-scale-refused.ts`, the D2 conversion `form-view-subform-columns-canonicalized` in `conversions/registry.ts`, and the head's check-runs. Tree facts were read with `git show` / `git grep` / `git diff` / `git log` against the fetched refs; nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run. The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's conclusions were read as comments on the card, not adopted.

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies**

1. No accept set moves, in either direction. The diff adds one element to the hand-written `STEP18_RATIONALE` list in `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` (+31) and one changeset (+10). No schema, conversion, entry, export, key or default is touched. The only published thing that changes is the VALUE of `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].rationale` — `step18.rationale` is `joinRationale(STEP18_RATIONALE)` (registry `:6054`), `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` is `{ 17: step17, 18: step18 }` (`:19161`), re-exported from `migrations/index.ts`, and ships in `dist/migrations/index.js` / `.mjs` (`package.json` `files[]` carries `dist`; the `./migrations` export resolves there). RIGHT: a longer string, no widening, no narrowing.
2. Placement and numbering, per the list's own header (`:5006-5022`) and `scripts/step18-rationale-merge.test.ts`. The id `form-view-subform-columns-closed` sits at position 25 of 54, between `form-view-option-default-retired` and `list-view-page-mount-retired`, which is where it sorts under the test's strict less-than string order on `id`; the whole list stays sorted and every id is kebab-case. `order` 54 is one above the highest at the dev's base `5dbeb7d7b7` (53 fragments, max order 53), and also one above the highest at the merge base `dff98c1f51` and at `origin/main` `fed0db8f69` as read 2026-10-01 (both 53 / 53), so the number is right against every base this PR can land on; the 54 orders are unique and contiguous. The element matches the test's `ELEMENT` regex exactly (the `id` / `order` / `text:` lines and six-space-indented text lines, closed by `  },`): parsing the head's file with that regex yields 54 elements and the `];` residue the test demands; the text has no leading or trailing space; it renders last, after `cube-member-sql-expression-retired` (53). RIGHT.
3. Generated regions. The diff holds one hunk, at `:5507`, outside every os-generated marker — as the file header (`:37-42`) says the step rationale is hand-written. Emulating `build-migration-registry.ts`'s `renderRegion` by text (comment lines verbatim at four spaces, the literal at four spaces with its trailing semicolon swapped for a comma, entries sorted by id within major) over every entry file at the head and comparing against the six regions in the head's file: semantic:17 (77 entries), semantic:18 (256), retired-key:17 (29), retired-key:18 (213), retired-def:17 (53), retired-def:18 (158) — all six byte-identical, and the totals (333 / 242 / 211) are the dev's. Both #20901 entries and the declared-type entry are in the semantic:18 region, byte-identical to their sources. CI: `check:migration-registry` runs in `Lint & Repo Gates` and `check:upgrade-guide` in `Type Check · source gates`; both green. RIGHT — the generator is a no-op on this diff.
4. No pin names this fragment by id. The merge test pins the list's shape, sort, order integrity and the joined paragraph, not any one fragment; that is the list's design for every fragment, and the dev's ablation (fragment deleted, every leg green) is what that design predicts. Noted under ③, not a defect of this PR.

**The fragment, sentence by sentence.** Author-shown: `os migrate meta --step` prints `hop.rationale` under `── protocol 18 ──` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:428-430`) and `--json` carries it per hop (`:662-668`); the default terminus is `CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR = max(PROTOCOL_MAJOR, ...MIGRATION_MAJORS)` = 18 (`:89`, `:606`). The generated upgrade guide does not print it today (`build-upgrade-guide.ts:78` loops to `PROTOCOL_MAJOR`, and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `17.0.0`). Every sentence below is judged at the head, which is `main` plus this fragment, so "true" means true on `main` the moment this PR lands.

- S1 "It also closes the form view's inline grid columns: `subforms[].columns`, on `view.form` and on `formViews` entries, was `z.array(z.any())` while a relationship field's `inlineColumns` was already the strict `InlineGridColumnSchema`, so a mis-keyed column published clean and drew a blank grid column, and `scale` on a currency column, which the other carrier refuses under the maintainer's rulings of 2026-09-23 (option B) and 2026-09-24 (option 乙), published green." TRUE, since `bee75cebe6`. Sources: the entry `:5-7` (the two carriers), `:17` (surface: `view.form` and each `formViews` entry), `:26-29` (mis-keyed column published clean and drew a blank grid column; `scale` on a currency column refused on the other carrier under those two rulings, green here); the conversion docblock (`conversions/registry.ts:9844-9845`, "`z.array(z.any())` through 17.5.0"); `field.zod.ts`'s `INLINE_GRID_COLUMN_HISTORY` ("rendered as blank cells"); and the card's own measurement of 17.5.0. The two dates are the entries' own words (both entries carry them); `field.zod.ts` cites the same rulings by comment id (`5791803339` on #19629, letter B; `5805782503` on #19910, letter 乙) and the dates are not re-read here. One register nuance, not a falsity: ruling B retired `scale` from the currency FIELD type and 乙 worded the remedy; the column mirror's refusal is triage's carry of both (declared-type entry `:22-23`), and "refuses under the maintainer's rulings" is the identity-only entry's own phrasing (`:25-27`). "the other carrier refuses" is present tense inside a past-tense clause; it is true then and now.
- S2 "The carrier now references that schema, so both carriers are judged by it, with its own prescriptions." TRUE: `view.zod.ts:4399` `columns: z.array(InlineGridColumnSchema)` with the #20901 comment above it; the entry `:8-9`, `:30-31`.
- S3 "The D2 conversion `form-view-subform-columns-canonicalized` respells a `{ field }` column as `{ name }`, the respelling `field-column-lists-canonicalized` makes on `inlineColumns`: it rewrites stored rows and assembled artifacts and lists the edit under `os migrate meta`, and it is retired from the load path, so an author writing `field` meets the refusal." TRUE. The entry at `:9877-9881` (`toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.5.0'`) and `field-column-lists-canonicalized` (`:7700`) both call the one `respellInlineGridColumns` (`:7639-7656`: a dict with a string `field` and no `name` has the key renamed, every other key kept). Stored rows: `conversions/stored.ts` replays the full chain with `includeRetired: true` (`:17`, `:104`), and the conversion walks every form payload `mapViewPayloads` reaches. Assembled artifacts: the conversion's own `viewItems` walk, and the artifact door replays a retired entry when the floor is below the runtime label or at or below the entry's `retiredAfter` (`artifact-forward-conversion.ts:37`; ADR-0087 amended 2026-09-30) — with the label at 17.5.0 and `retiredAfter` 17.5.0 every artifact that can carry `field` is inside the window, and a floor above 17.5.0 cannot carry it, so the clause holds at every moment. Listed under `os migrate meta`: `step18.conversionIds` is derived from `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR[18]`, which lists the entry at order 51, and `conversions/apply.ts:58` says `applyMetaMigrations` applies the chain directly; `os migrate meta` is the house spelling (44 occurrences in the registry's strings). Load path: `includeRetired` defaults to false at the authoring doors (`apply.ts:34`) and the column schema's alias table refuses `field` with the prescription naming `name`.
- S4 "A view saved with a failing column is refused with the column schema's prescription, and a stored row carrying one is diagnosed at rehydration; neither is stripped, because which column an unknown key or a mixed `field`/`name` entry meant is the author's call, and a conversion that dropped the key would accept at load what the parse now refuses." TRUE: the entry `:12-14`, `:34-35`; ADR-0087 addendum 2026-07-31 ("Writes stay gated; reads diagnose, never drop": `saveMetaItem` 422; `loadMetaFromDb` warns `[metadata_spec_invalid]` and registers the row anyway); `respellInlineGridColumns` returns a both-keys entry by reference (`'name' in entry`), and the conversion's fixture carries `{ field: 'amount', name: 'total' }` untouched in `after`.
- S5 "Its D3 record is the semantic entry `form-view-subform-columns-closed`." TRUE: entry `:16`; semantic:18 region `:6052`. The phrase is the list's own — three other fragments say "Its D3 record is the semantic entry".
- S6 "On both carriers, the reach of `inline-grid-column-currency-scale-refused` extends to a column that declares no `type`: such a column takes its type from the child field, which the column schema cannot see, when the console hydrates it, so `defineStack`'s cross-reference check re-parses a column whose `name` is a `currency` field of the child object as the type it renders as, and the refusal of its `scale` is the column schema's own." TRUE: `stack.zod.ts:2720-2786` — `collectHydratedInlineColumnErrors`, called from `validateCrossReferences` (`:2855`), walks every field's `inlineColumns` and every `subforms[]` of `view.form` and of each `formViews` entry, skips a column that declares `type`, resolves the child field's type through `HYDRATED_INLINE_COLUMN_TYPE` (one row, `currency`), re-parses `{ ...column, type: resolved }` with `InlineGridColumnSchema.safeParse` and reports each issue's own message. "when the console hydrates it" is the identity-only entry `:7-8` and `stack.zod.ts`'s pin citation (`hydrateColumns` at `.objectui-sha` `db11afd4967c`) — an objectui reading outside this record's inputs, consistent with the `field.zod.ts` superRefine comment; UNSOURCED here, under-reach only if wrong. "the child object": for `inlineColumns` the column names a field of the object that owns the relationship field (`judge(field.inlineColumns, obj.name, …)`), which the schema places on the child — the family's term, as the identity-only entry's surface uses it.
- S7 "Reach: the child object must be declared in the same stack; a column naming no field of it, or a subform whose child object comes from another package, is not judged there." TRUE, verbatim from the identity-only entry `:32-34`, and what the code does: `fieldsByObject` is built from `config.objects` alone, `judge` returns on a missing child object or a missing field, and this check never consults `artifactObjects` (the `validateCrossReferences` docblock: the two artifact-scoped classes only). "Reach:" as a sentence opener is new to the fragment list but is both entries' own register.
- S8 "It has no D2 conversion, for the declared-type entry's reason: deleting the key is the migration, and a conversion that dropped it would accept it at load, the grace window ruling B refused." TRUE: zero hits for `identity-only` or `currency-scale-refused` in `conversions/registry.ts` at the head; the identity-only entry `:11-13`, `:20`; the declared-type entry `:24-27` ("No alias and no grace window, per ruling B. NOT mechanically converted"); `field.zod.ts`'s superRefine comment ("No alias and no grace window (ruling B's own words)"). Ruling B here is the 2026-09-23 ruling S1 names — consistent.
- S9 "Its D3 record is the semantic entry `inline-grid-column-identity-only-currency-scale-refused`." TRUE: entry `:15`; region `:6534`.

Nothing over-broad was found; the one unsourced clause is the objectui hydration reading in S6, sourced to the entry and the pin citation. Does the fragment say anything the rulings it cites did not rule? No. It attributes exactly two things to maintainer rulings — the currency `scale` refusal (B, 乙) and the grace-window refusal (B) — exactly as the entries and `field.zod.ts` attribute them. The carrier closure, the D2 vehicle (`retiredAfter` 17.5.0, the sibling id) and the identity-only reach extension are stated as facts of the code and the entries, which they are; they were triage and seat decisions on #20901 (`5916820410`, `5918621378`, `5920724494`) and the fragment claims no ruling for them. It restates no population count, no `retiredAfter` reasoning and no objectui-mirror status — correctly left to the entries and the conversion docblock. Register against its neighbours: it opens "It also …" like its render neighbours (orders 52 and 53), names the D2 conversion and the D3 entries the way `cube-refresh-key-retired` and `cube-member-sql-expression-retired` do, and cites rulings by date and option letter rather than by tracker number. Every neighbour carries a tracker number ("(#9227)", "(#17063, …)", "(#12868, …)") and this fragment carries none; that is what AGENTS.md `:16-17` asks of author-shown runtime strings, so the neighbours are the deviation (the dev's second out-of-scope finding). It is longer (about 2.4 KB against 1.2-1.6 KB for most neighbours) because one fragment carries two D3 entries and a D2 conversion — the shape the at-tier item 4 asked for, with `duration-keys-unit-in-key` as the per-family precedent.

**The changeset** `.changeset/20901-step18-rationale-form-view-subform-columns.md`, sentence by sentence. Frontmatter `'@objectstack/spec': patch` — see ②. The title "fix(spec): protocol 18's migration rationale now covers the form view's inline grid columns and the identity-only currency `scale` refusal (#20901)" — true; a tracker number in CHANGELOG text is the house form, not a runtime string. "`MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].rationale` gains one fragment, `form-view-subform-columns-closed`." TRUE (item 1 above). "It is the paragraph `os migrate meta --step` shows for the protocol 17 → 18 hop." TRUE (`meta.ts:428-430`). "The new sentences say that a form view's `subforms[].columns` now takes the strict `InlineGridColumnSchema` a relationship field's `inlineColumns` takes, that the conversion … respells a `{ field }` column as `{ name }` in stored rows and assembled artifacts while an author writing `field` is refused, and that `defineStack` refuses `scale` on a column that declares no `type` when its `name` is a `currency` field of a child object declared in the same stack (…)." TRUE — an accurate précis of S2, S3, S6 and S7. "Text only: no schema, conversion or migration entry changes, and `conversionIds` and `semantic` for step 18 are unchanged." TRUE: `conversionIds` is derived from an untouched `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR`, and the semantic region is byte-identical to the merge base.

**The PR body**, sentence by sentence. "Part of #20901" and "Clause-②: no" — right (② below; the Part-of guard is green and the card is open). "`order` 54 (the highest at base `5dbeb7d7b7` was 53), inserted where its id sorts" — TRUE (item 2). "It covers the form-view carrier closure, the D2 conversion …, and the identity-only sibling …" — TRUE. "Each sentence restates the two entry sources and the conversion source." TRUE, with the S6 nuance (the hydration clause is the entry's, which rests on the pin citation). "The list sits outside the generated markers and is hand-written; `gen:migration-registry` is a no-op on this diff." TRUE (item 3). "A `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/spec` is included because the rationale string ships in `dist/migrations`." TRUE (item 1). "This is review item 4 of the at-tier record `5921114874` on #20953." TRUE. "The card stays open, and the seat closes it by hand." TRUE at the read. Verification section: the counts (31, 179, 588 files / 17318, typecheck, 15 artifacts, 82 derived) and the ablation are the dev's own runs, not re-run here; the check-runs below stand for the CI-visible families (`Test Core` runs `test` and `test:repo`, which holds `step18-rationale-merge.test.ts`; `Lint & Repo Gates` holds `check:migration-registry`; `Type Check · source gates` holds `check:upgrade-guide`). "The upgrade guide prints majors up to `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` (17), so it does not print step 18 and has no diff here." TRUE. "no pin went red … no test pins this fragment by id" — consistent with the test file. Acceptance notes: "207 of 253 at `06f079864a`" is quoted from the review record; at this head it is 208 of 256 semantic:18 entries without a fragment of their own id (54 fragments, six of which are family ids that are not an entry id — `compliance-deadline-keys-retired`, `cron-positions-deleted`, `duration-keys-unit-in-key`, `element-filter-retired`, `element-form-retired`, `page-component-filter-record-to-rule-array`). "Fragments are per retirement family, so the number of families without one is not counted." TRUE. "`carrier:` none named." TRUE. "The generated guide prints major 17 only" — TRUE. "Step 18's rationale does reach `os migrate meta --step`, whose default chain ends at major 18" — TRUE (`CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR` = 18 at this head since `MIGRATION_MAJORS` is [17, 18]). "There, a family without a fragment is left out of the paragraph, not misstated." TRUE by construction of `joinRationale`. "This was read from the source and not measured at that door." — honest; this record reads the same source and measures nothing at the door either.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no

`'@objectstack/spec': patch`, title `fix(spec):`, `Clause-②: no` with no arm — matches what the diff publishes. The only published change is a longer string value in `dist/migrations` (the `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].rationale` paragraph). No export is added, removed or renamed (`STEP18_RATIONALE` and `joinRationale` are module-private; the Type Check family that carries `check:api-surface` is green), no accept set widens or narrows, no key is added to any payload. AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist step 3: anything that publishes takes a changeset, a fix in a released package takes `patch`, never none and never `skip-changeset` — the string ships in the tarball, so a changeset is owed and `patch` is its level. In `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`'s terms the body's line `Clause-②: no` is key-initial, its value token is `no` and no parenthetical follows, so `readClause2Line` returns `declared`, value `no`, arm `null`; the question the value answers (does this card widen an accept set or the public surface) is no for a text-only addition to a shipped string, and the absent arm is right because nothing narrows — `(narrowing)` would declare a break that does not exist, and `yes` would force `minor` for a widening that does not exist. No `**BREAKING**` banner and no ADR-0087 marker, correctly, since the changeset declares no break. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
